item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong evidence of some course correction in economic management, welfare delivery, procurement, cabinet composition, and the minors case. I did not find an independent 2024 evaluation showing whether those corrections materially improved nationwide outcomes by year-end. The clearest unresolved gap is whether the late corrections were durable or mostly reactive damage control after the protests and backlash.","evidence":[{"title":"The government resumed cash transfers to vulnerable households after reform shock","publisher":"Reuters via MarketScreener","date":"2024-02-26","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Nigeria-restarts-cash-transfers-to-cushion-hardship-caused-by-reforms-46031196/","summary":"Nigeria resumed direct cash transfers to 12 million vulnerable households to cushion hardship from subsidy removal and currency devaluation. This is strong evidence of reallocating resources after the initial reform shock became politically and socially costly.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.7","8B.6"]},{"title":"Tinubu created a technocratic macro-coordination structure to drive implementation","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-03-27","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/","summary":"Tinubu set up the PECC and EET, centered on the finance minister and CBN governor and including economists and private-sector figures, with rapid implementation and monitoring duties. That is strong evidence of adapting method and tightening execution rather than leaving the reform program on autopilot.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"Tinubu ordered monthly welfare reporting and faster delivery","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-02-22","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/","summary":"He ordered faster welfare processing and monthly KPI reporting for vulnerable-citizen interventions. This shows a clear attempt to correct delivery bottlenecks after recognizing that relief needed tighter administrative control.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"The student-loan pledge became a standing delivery structure","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-04-04","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/","summary":"The student-loan agenda was converted into law and a standing institution, NELFUND, rather than left as campaign rhetoric. That is evidence of adapting the program into an implementable mechanism.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"Tinubu reorganized procurement leadership","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-06-15","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/","summary":"Tinubu directed the BPP chief to resign as part of a broader reorganization to improve efficiency and transparency. This is direct evidence of replacing or retooling an implementer after deciding the old setup was inadequate.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6"]},{"title":"Tinubu reshuffled the cabinet after months of pressure","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-10-23","url":"https://theprint.in/world/nigerias-tinubu-names-seven-ministers-sacks-five-in-cabinet-reshuffle/2325625/","summary":"Reuters reported that Tinubu sacked five ministers, reassigned ten, appointed seven new ones, and kept finance, defence, and planning in place. This is strong evidence of course correction in the executive team, especially at the delivery-critical economic core.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.7","8B.6"]},{"title":"Tinubu ordered a probe and release of detained minors after public backlash","publisher":"TheCable","date":"2024-11-04","url":"https://www.thecable.ng/tinubu-orders-probe-of-security-agents-involved-in-arrest-detention-of-minors/","summary":"After the protest crackdown, Tinubu ordered an investigation into the arrest and treatment of detained minors, with possible discipline for officers. This is the clearest late-year corrective action and shows he could reverse course when abuse became politically costly.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"UNICEF confirmed the release order for detained children","publisher":"UNICEF Nigeria","date":"2024-11-05","url":"https://www.unicef.org/nigeria/press-releases/unicef-welcomes-president-tinubus-order-immediate-release-detained-children","summary":"UNICEF said Tinubu directed the release of all children and young persons detained over the protests. This corroborates a real corrective step, though it was reactive rather than preventive.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"The government framed the protest response as dialogue plus deployment","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-07-31","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462","summary":"Reuters reported the government offered dialogue while security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence, but it does show some attempt to preserve control through negotiation as well as coercion.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"Security-law escalation kept going despite reforms","publisher":"CPJ","date":"2024-10-03","url":"https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/","summary":"CPJ reported four journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite February reforms, showing the administration had not fully corrected its legal pressure on scrutiny. This is negative evidence that correction was selective and incomplete.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"Treason charges against protesters show punitive non-correction","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-11-01","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000","summary":"Reuters reported 76 people, including minors, were charged with treason and inciting a military coup after August protests. That is strong negative evidence: instead of correcting course toward restraint, the state escalated to a harsher legal strategy.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"Amnesty documented the crackdown as coercive rather than corrected","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-11-28","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/","summary":"Amnesty reported killings, mass detentions, and torture during the August crackdown. This is strong negative evidence that the state did not timely correct the coercive trajectory once it became visible.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]},{"title":"Counterevidence on procurement and information control remains strong","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House said the Cybercrimes Act remained a tool for legal pressure, intimidation, and self-censorship, even after amendment. That suggests Tinubu did not fully correct the state’s information-control tools.","question_ids":["8B.8","8B.6","8B.7"]}]}
